pib.criterio: annual rate of change calculated from the sum of the four quarters of the chained volume index for the current year over the sum of the four quarters of the previous year (equivalent to the "cumulative change in the year" published by the IBGE); for 2026, the 1st and 2nd quarters combined over the same period of 2025, since there is not yet data for the full year

fonte.nome: IBGE - Sistema de Contas Nacionais Trimestrais, Tabela SIDRA 1620

notas.nota: The values in this series use the most recent version of the chained volume index of GDP, which incorporates the changes of base year/reference of the National Accounts made by IBGE in 2007 (2000 reference), in 2015 (2010 reference) and in 2024 (2021 reference, incorporating data from the 2022 Censo). These revisions retroactively change the annual rates of change; for that reason, some values here may differ from the figures originally released in the quarterly releases of each period.
The 2026 figure is partial: cumulative change in the 1st and 2nd quarters of 2026 against the same period in 2025. There is not yet a full-year result.

bpc.orgao: Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS) — Secretaria Nacional de Assistência Social (SNAS), Departamento de Benefícios Assistenciais (DBA)
bpc.serie_codigo: VIS DATA 3 (SAGICAD/MDS) — 'Benefício de Prestação Continuada BPC - por município pagador' (base de dados Maciça / Base de Dados Agentes Pagadores)
bpc.criterio: Total number of people receiving the BPC/LOAS in Brazil in December of each year (the last month of the year; see the 2026 exception in the notes), adding the two categories under which the source publishes the data: elderly people (65 or over) and people with disabilities (PCD). It is a count of beneficiaries with a payment made in that month (payroll base — SINTESE/INSS through 2018, Maciça from Jan/2019 on), not the total of grants/applications in the year nor a subset registered in the Cadastro Único. The series does not distinguish, within each month, entries and exits (deaths, terminations, new grants), only the stock of beneficiaries paid in that month.

fonte.nome: MDS — VIS DATA 3 (Secretaria de Avaliação, Gestão da Informação e Cadastro Único), 'Benefício de Prestação Continuada BPC - por município pagador'

notas.nota: The series begins in 2004: it is the first year with monthly data on beneficiaries (PCD and elderly) available in this VIS DATA base ('BPC por município pagador'), which is the only source found, within the data collection time frame (September 2026), with an explicit historical series of the number of beneficiaries (and not only amounts transferred in reais) that can be queried by year. The BPC has existed since 1996 (Lei nº 8.742/1993 — LOAS — regulated in 1995/1996), but no series of the number of beneficiaries for 1996-2003 published by a primary source (INSS/MPS/MDS) with the same methodology as this base was found within that time frame; that is why 1998-2003 do not enter this series.

From January 2019 onward, the source of the data on the municipality of payment changed from the Sistema SINTESE (INSS) to the 'Maciça' database (Previdência Social payroll), according to the metadata of the dataset itself. The series shows no visible discontinuity in the national aggregate figures around that date, but the change of source system is recorded here as a possible methodological break.
The year 2026 is incomplete: the figure shown is for July 2026 (the most recent reference month available in the source on the collection date, September 2026), not December.

desmatamento.unidade: km² per year (PRODES survey year, August to July)
desmatamento.orgao: INPE — Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais
desmatamento.serie_codigo: PRODES (Programa de Cálculo do Desflorestamento da Amazônia) e PRODES Biomas / BiomasBR
desmatamento.criterio: total area of clear-cut deforestation detected by satellite in each crop year (1 August to 31 July), by biome; for the Amazônia, it refers to the Amazônia Legal (nine states); for Cerrado, Mata Atlântica and Pantanal, it refers to the biome polygon measured by the PRODES Biomas/BiomasBR system.

fonte.nome: INPE — TerraBrasilis / PRODES (painel de desmatamento por biomas)

notas.nota: start of the PRODES series for the Amazônia Legal (nine states: AC, AM, AP, MA, MT, PA, RO, RR, TO); it is the historical reference series of PRODES, calculated by clear-cutting of forest cover.
there was no independent annual survey for 1993 and 1994 because of the limited images available at the time; the INPE publishes the same value (14.896 km²) for both crop years.
start of PRODES monitoring for the Cerrado biome, with the first period measured from August/2000 to July/2002 (two years); the value is recorded in the final year of the period (2002).

start of PRODES monitoring for the Mata Atlântica and Pantanal biomes, with the first period measured from August/2000 to July/2004 (four years); the value is recorded in the final year of the period (2004).
the 'year' of each point corresponds to the PRODES survey year, which runs from August 1 of the previous year to July 31 of the year shown — not to the calendar year (January to December).
PRODES Cerrado begins to measure an annual period (Aug-Jul) from crop year 2012/2013; before that the periods were two-year (2000/2002, 2002/2004, 2004/2006, 2006/2008, 2008/2010, 2010/2012).

PRODES Mata Atlântica and PRODES Pantanal begin to measure an annual period (Aug-Jul) from crop year 2016/2017; before that the periods were irregular: 2000/2004 (4 years), 2004/2006, 2006/2008, 2008/2010 (two-year periods), 2010/2011 (1 year), 2011/2013 (two-year period) and 2013/2014 (1 year), 2014/2016 (two-year period).

for the data points referring to multi-year periods (for example, Cerrado 2002 and 2004; Mata Atlântica and Pantanal 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2013, 2016), the value is the total measured for the whole period and is attributed to the final year of the period, not to a rate for a single year; years within those periods that are not the final year have no confirmed individual value and for that reason appear as null.

the 'Amazônia' category refers to the Amazônia Legal (an administrative area of nine states used by PRODES since 1988), which is the reference historical series released annually by INPE; it does not correspond to the strict polygon of the Amazônia biome, monitored separately by PRODES Biomas since 2007/2008 with different results.

the most recent confirmed figure is crop year 2024/2025 (August 2024 to July 2025), released by the INPE/PRODES in 2025-2026; there is no confirmed figure for crop year 2025/2026 up to the collection date (September 2026).

homicidios.orgao: Ipea / Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública (FBSP)
homicidios.criterio: Rate of 'homicides', defined by the Atlas da Violência as the sum of deaths by assault (ICD-10 X85-Y09) and deaths by legal intervention (ICD-10 Y35-Y36), recorded in the Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (SIM/Ministério da Saúde), divided by the population estimated by IBGE, per 100,000 inhabitants, Brazil. This is a different definition from that of 'Mortes Violentas Intencionais' (MVI) used by the Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública/FBSP, which is measured from state police records and adds together intentional homicide, femicide, robbery followed by death, bodily harm followed by death and death by police intervention as distinct categories; the FBSP's MVI series only begins in 2012 and produces numbers and rates different from those presented here for the same years. The Atlas da Violência 'homicides' series was chosen because it has longer historical coverage.

fonte.nome: Ipea/FBSP — Atlas da Violência, edições anuais 2016 a 2026 (dados SIM/Ministério da Saúde e população IBGE)

notas.nota: The series begins in 2004: it was the earliest year for which a national homicide rate explicitly published in an edition of the Atlas da Violência (nota técnica nº 17, Atlas da Violência 2016) was found within the search carried out. Years before 2004 did not enter for lack of direct confirmation in a primary source within the data collection time frame (September 2026); this does not mean that data for earlier years do not exist in SIM/DATASUS, only that a consolidated national rate published by the Atlas da Violência for 1998-2003 was not found.

The Atlas da Violência periodically revises the entire historical series with each new edition (among other reasons, because of updates to IBGE population projections, including after the 2022 Census). As a result, the same year appears with slightly different rates depending on the edition: for example, 2012 appears as 29.4 in the 2017/2020 edition and as 28.9 in the 2024 edition (the most recent); 2018 appears as 27.8 in the 2020 edition and as 27.9 in the 2024 edition. In this series, for each year the value from the most recent edition of the Atlas da Violência that publishes it is used, as available up to the collection date (September 2026); small differences of a tenth relative to older editions of the Atlas, or to news reports based on them, are therefore expected and do not indicate a collection error.

The 2023 figure (21.2) is the one published in the Atlas da Violência 2025 edition (base year 2023), with 45,747 homicides. The following edition, Atlas da Violência 2026 (base year 2024), returned to 2023 only indirectly, reporting that the 2024 rate (20.1) represents a 7.4% drop from 2023 — which would imply a 2023 rate close to 21.7, and not 21.2; in the sources consulted, that new edition did not publish a closed, explicit figure for 2023 to replace the 21.2. The value of 21.2, directly published, is kept here, with the divergence recorded.

The 2024 figure (20,1 per 100,000, 42.590 homicides) comes from the most recent edition of the Atlas da Violência (2026), released in May 2026. It is the last year with a national homicide rate published by the Atlas da Violência up to the date of this collection (September 2026); the Atlas is usually released about two years after the reference year of the data, so an edition covering 2025 was not expected before 2027.

ideb.titulo: Ideb — Índice de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica, public schools
ideb.orgao: INEP — Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira
ideb.serie_codigo: Ideb (Saeb + taxa de aprovação do Censo Escolar), edições 2007 a 2025
ideb.criterio: Ideb of the public school system (state, municipal and federal schools combined; excludes private schools), Brazil, at the three stages assessed: the early years of primary school (5th grade), the final years of primary school (9th grade) and secondary school (3rd year). The Ideb is calculated every 2 years (odd-numbered years), combining average proficiency in Portuguese Language and Mathematics measured by the Saeb with the pass rate from the Censo Escolar da Educação Básica, on a scale of 0 to 10.

fonte.nome: INEP — Ideb, resultados por edição (2007 a 2025), rede pública Brasil

notas.nota: The Ideb was created in 2007 and has its first reference edition in 2005; since then it has been released every 2 years (2005, 2007, 2009, ... 2025). This series begins in 2007, not in 2005: the 2005 values widely cited in the press and in publicity material (3.8 for early grades; 3.5 for later grades; 3.4 for secondary education) are national in scope, combining the public and private networks, not the public network alone — no official and readily verifiable breakdown of the 2005 Ideb for the public network alone across the three stages, compatible with the criterion used in the rest of this series, was located within the collection deadline (September 2026). For that reason 2005 does not enter as a data point in this series.

The 2021 edition kept the biennial frequency (no edition was skipped because of the Covid-19 pandemic), but the Saeb 2021 was administered in November 2021, later than usual, amid school interruptions linked to the pandemic. The early years and secondary school show a decline or stagnation between 2019 and 2021 in this series, coinciding with that period.
2025 is the most recent edition available on the collection date (September 2026), released in August 2026, and it is the highest value in the series in all three stages.

pontos.obs: see note on the Saeb being administered during the pandemic
highest values in the series in all stages

bolsa_familia.titulo: Bolsa Família — beneficiary families and average benefit value
bolsa_familia.unidade: mixed unit: millions of families / current reais
bolsa_familia.orgao: Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS) — Secretaria Nacional de Renda e Cidadania (Senarc)
bolsa_familia.serie_codigo: VIS DATA 3 (SAGICAD/MDS) — 'Programa Bolsa Família - número de famílias beneficiárias, valores totais repassados e valor médio do benefício' e 'Programa Auxílio Brasil - quantidade de famílias e valores do Auxílio Brasil'
bolsa_familia.criterio: Category 'Beneficiary families': number of families that received the benefit in December of each year (the last month of the year; see exceptions in the notes), converted to millions of families (rounded to 2 decimal places) from the absolute number reported by VIS DATA/MDS. Category 'Average benefit amount': average monthly benefit amount per family (Demonstrativo Físico/Financeiro), in current reais of the reference month (December of each year, except where the notes indicate otherwise) — it is not an amount accumulated over the year nor adjusted for inflation; the same nominal amount from different years is not directly comparable in purchasing power. The series covers, under the same identifier 'bolsa_familia', three phases of the same federal income-transfer program for low-income families, which changed name and design over time (see notes): Bolsa Família (2003 to Oct/2021), Auxílio Brasil (Nov/2021 to Feb/2023) and Bolsa Família, with a renewed design (from Mar/2023). Each point indicates, in 'obs', what the program's name was in that year's reference month.

fonte.nome: MDS — VIS DATA 3 (Secretaria de Avaliação, Gestão da Informação e Cadastro Único), Demonstrativo Físico/Financeiro do Bolsa Família e do Auxílio Brasil

notas.nota: The program changed name and design over the course of the series: it was called 'Bolsa Família' from 2003 to October 2021; it was renamed 'Auxílio Brasil' between November 2021 and February 2023 (Law No. 14,284/2021); and it went back to being called 'Bolsa Família', with revised rules and amounts, from March 2023 onward (Law No. 14,601/2023). The 2021 figure in this series (reference month: October 2021) is the last month still under the name 'Bolsa Família' before the change; the 2022 figure (reference month: December 2022) is already 'Auxílio Brasil'; from 2023 onward, the figures (reference month: December, except 2026) are from Bolsa Família in its post-2023 design. Families receiving benefits under one program do not migrate automatically one-for-one to the next in these transitions, and the benefit calculation rules changed in each of them; comparisons of average amounts between different phases of the program must be made with caution.

Between April and December 2020, most of the families eligible for Bolsa Família received the Auxílio Emergencial (created in response to the Covid-19 pandemic) instead of the regular Bolsa Família benefit, or as a top-up to it when the Auxílio Emergencial was larger. The Auxílio Emergencial was a separate program, outside Bolsa Família, and is not included in this series. For that reason, the average Bolsa Família benefit amount recorded here for December 2020 (R$ 29.74) and for October 2021 (R$ 87.50, when a new Auxílio Emergencial 2021 was also in force between March and October 2021) reflect only the residual amount paid by Bolsa Família in those months to the families that remained in the program, and are much lower than the average amount in years without overlap with the Auxílio Emergencial — they do not indicate a real fall in the typical benefit received by families in those two years.

There is, in the sources consulted, no consolidated and directly published annual figure for beneficiary families or average benefit value for 2023 covering the whole year under a single program design (the year combines 2 months of Auxílio Brasil and 10 months of the new Bolsa Família). The 2023 data point of this series uses the month of December/2023 (already under the new Bolsa Família), on the same criterion applied to the other years.
The year 2026 is incomplete: the figure shown is for the month of August 2026 (the most recent reference month available in VIS DATA on the collection date, September 2026), not December.

Amounts in current reais of each reference month, with no correction for inflation. A series of the average benefit value adjusted by a price index (e.g.: INPC/IPCA) would produce a different path from the one shown here.

mortalidade_causas.titulo: Mortality in Brazil by broad cause group
mortalidade_causas.orgao: Ministério da Saúde/SVS — Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (SIM), IBGE (população)
mortalidade_causas.serie_codigo: IDB — Indicadores e Dados Básicos para a Saúde (RIPSA/DATASUS/Ministério da Saúde), 2ª edição revisada, indicadores C.8 (circulatório) e C.9 (causas externas)
mortalidade_causas.criterio: Specific mortality rate (number of deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, both sexes, total resident population), Brazil, calculated from SIM deaths (Ministério da Saúde) and IBGE population, following the methodology of the IDB (Indicadores e Dados Básicos para a Saúde no Brasil), a joint publication of RIPSA/Ministério da Saúde/DATASUS. 'Diseases of the circulatory system' = ICD-10 chapter IX (includes ischemic heart diseases and cerebrovascular diseases). 'External causes' = ICD-10 chapter XX (accidents, assaults/homicides, self-inflicted injuries/suicides, and other external causes of morbidity and mortality); it is a broader group than the 'homicidios' series of this collection, which covers only part of the external causes.

fonte.nome: IDB — Indicadores e Dados Básicos para a Saúde no Brasil (RIPSA/Ministério da Saúde/DATASUS), 2ª edição revisada, fichas C.8 e C.9

notas.nota: It was not possible to confirm values for 1998-1999, nor for most of the years between the data points presented here (1990, 2000, 2004): the IDB publication, which is the source with mortality rates specific by major cause group and per 100,000 inhabitants already calculated and published for Brazil as a whole, provides, in its 2nd revised edition, only the base years 1990, 2000 and 2004 for these indicators. The years between those points were neither interpolated nor filled in.

It was not possible to extend this series beyond 2004: the IDB publication (RIPSA/DATASUS), which provided these indicators already calculated as a rate per 100,000 inhabitants, was discontinued around 2012, and the most recent editions located do not repeat these indicators under the same codes. DATASUS keeps the raw SIM data up to date (including for recent years, 2023-2026), accessible through the interactive TabNet tool (general mortality, http://tabnet.datasus.gov.br), but that tool requires an interactive query (selection of ICD-10 chapter, year, and cross-tabulation with population) that could not be completed within the collection deadline (September 2026) with direct confirmation from a primary source for recent years. For that reason no data points between 2005 and 2026 appear in this series.

No category was included in this series for Covid-19 (which only exists as a cause of death from 2020 onwards), nor for neoplasms (cancer) or diseases of the respiratory system, although they were foreseen in the initial scope: no mortality rate for Brazil (both sexes, total population) per 100,000 inhabitants, already published by an official source with a clear methodology and compatible with the criterion of this series, was located within the collection period for those three categories. For neoplasms, source C.10 of the IDB only publishes rates specific by sex and by tumour location (not a total rate for all neoplasms, both sexes); for respiratory diseases and Covid-19, no ready-made table equivalent to that of C.8/C.9 was located. Absolute Covid-19 deaths in Brazil are widely reported by the Ministério da Saúde (coronavirus.saude.gov.br dashboard), but obtaining a count of deaths per calendar year (not cumulative) with an exact cut-off date, and the corresponding rate per 100,000 inhabitants, would require a query that was not completed with direct confirmation within the period of this collection.

demarcacoes.titulo: Indigenous lands ratified by year or administration period
demarcacoes.orgao: FUNAI / Ministério dos Povos Indígenas — com comparação de contagens do ISA (Instituto Socioambiental) e do Cimi (Conselho Indigenista Missionário)
demarcacoes.serie_codigo: Homologações por decreto presidencial de Terras Indígenas, conforme Decreto nº 1.775/1996
demarcacoes.criterio: number of Terras Indígenas that reached the final stage of the demarcation process — ratification by decree of the President of the Republic — in the year or administration period indicated. It does not include land that has only been identified, declared (declaratory ordinance of the Ministério da Justiça) or only registered with a notary office/SPU without ratification; those are earlier or later stages, distinct from this one, of the same process.

fonte.nome: FUNAI/Ministério dos Povos Indígenas (balanços oficiais) e Cimi — Relatório Violência Contra os Povos Indígenas no Brasil (edições anuais); comparação histórica por governo com dados do ISA

notas.nota: for the period from 1995 to 2018 (the FHC, Lula 1st and 2nd terms, Dilma and Temer administrations), the sources consulted provide only the total ratified per administration, with no year-by-year breakdown; for that reason the value of each of these periods is recorded in the final year of the respective term, and not in each individual year.

for the period of Lula's 1st and 2nd terms (2003-2010), the Instituto Socioambiental (ISA) counts 87 indigenous lands ratified, while the Cimi counts 79; the value adopted in this series (87) is the ISA's. The difference between the two counts was not clarified in the sources consulted.
the Temer administration period counted as August 2016 to December 2018, corresponding to the effective length of the term after the impeachment of Dilma Rousseff.

no indigenous land was ratified in any of the four years of the Bolsonaro administration (2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022), according to the annual reports of the Cimi and the summaries of the ISA; this is why the series shows a value of 0 individually for each of those four years.
from 2023 onward (Lula administration, 3rd term), annual reports are published that make it possible to record the number of ratifications year by year.

pontos.obs: total for the 1995-2002 period (two terms of Fernando Henrique Cardoso), with no year-by-year breakdown in the sources consulted.

populacao.titulo: Brazil's population by broad age group and sex
populacao.criterio: Resident population projected for Brazil (1 July of each year), by sex and single year of age, aggregated here into three brackets from the SIDRA five-year age groups: '0 to 14 years' and '60 years or over' add men and women together; the '15 to 59 years' bracket is presented separately by sex. Source: SIDRA table 7358 ('População, por sexo e idade'), variable 606, year code C1933, Brazil (N1). This table contains the 2018 revision of IBGE's Projeção da População (last update recorded in SIDRA: 08/12/2020); IBGE released a more recent revision (2024, incorporating the results of the 2022 Census) in August 2024, but that revision was not found available as a SIDRA table that can be queried by sex and single year of age at the time of collection — see note. The SIDRA table only has data from the year 2000 onwards; it was not possible to confirm 1998 and 1999 in this source, and for that reason the series begins in 2000.

fonte.nome: IBGE - Projeção da População (revisão 2018), SIDRA tabela 7358

notas.nota: There is no confirmed figure for 1998 and 1999: SIDRA table 7358 (Projeção da População por sexo e idade) only covers from the year 2000. The series presented here starts in 2000, every 2 years, up to 2026.

The values in this series come from the 2018 revision of IBGE's Projeção da População, still indexed in SIDRA (table 7358) at the time of collection. IBGE published a 2024 revision (August 2024), which incorporates the results of the 2022 Censo Demográfico and tends to indicate a smaller total population than the 2018 revision projected for the same years (the 2022 Censo revealed slower population growth than expected). The figures in this series may therefore diverge from IBGE's most current official estimates for the same years; use them with that caveat, especially from 2022 on.
The 2026 figure is a projection (2018 revision), not an estimate based on a direct survey in that year.

reforma_agraria.titulo: Land reform — families settled and titles delivered
reforma_agraria.unidade: number of families / number of titles, by year
reforma_agraria.orgao: INCRA — Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária
reforma_agraria.serie_codigo: SIPRA (Sistema de Informações de Projetos de Reforma Agrária) — Relação de Projetos de Assentamento; balanços institucionais do INCRA para titulação
reforma_agraria.criterio: Settled families: number of families included in agrarian reform land settlement projects, summed by the project's year of creation (field 'DATA DE CRIACAO' of the SIPRA/INCRA register), from the public file 'Relação de projetos de assentamentos criados e reconhecidos pelo Incra'. Titles delivered: number of definitive titles of ownership (TD) or Concessions of Real Right of Use (CDRU) — the documents with the force of a public deed — delivered to settled families; it does not include Use Concession Contracts (CCU), a provisional administrative document with no registry value which, in official announcements, is sometimes added together with the definitive titles under the generic label of 'land titling'.

fonte.nome: INCRA — Relação de projetos de assentamentos criados e reconhecidos (SIPRA), arquivo aberto; e balanços institucionais do INCRA/Ministério do Desenvolvimento Agrário sobre titulação

notas.nota: the 'settled families' series begins in 1985, the year of the 1º Plano Nacional de Reforma Agrária, which marks the start of land settlement policy in a form close to the current one. The INCRA source file (SIPRA) contains scattered records of projects prior to 1985 (going back to 1930), not included in this series because they are fragmentary and predate the agrarian reform policy as institutionalized in the form in force today.

the 'settled families' figures for 2024 and, especially, 2025 are subject to upward revision: the source file (SIPRA/INCRA) was extracted on 06/03/2026, and there is a known lag between the date on which families are actually settled and the date the project is recorded/consolidated in the system. More recent years tend to be temporarily undercounted until the administrative processing is consolidated.

the year 2026 is not included in the 'settled families' series: the source file, extracted on 06/03/2026, records only 21 families for the year, reflecting only the first months and the start of administrative processing, not a confirmable annual total.

for 2017, the INCRA reported 'more than 26 thousand' definitive titles delivered to settlers (the exact number was not found, only the floor officially released); the value of 26.000 in this series represents that floor.

for the 2019-2022 period (Bolsonaro administration), the federal government announced the delivery of about 370,000 land titling documents to land reform settlers, of which INCRA itself and the specialized press indicated that only 12% were definitive titles (TD) or CDRU with the value of a deed — the remaining 88% were Contratos de Concessão de Uso (CCU), a provisional document. The 'titles delivered' figure recorded here for 2022 (44,400) is the result of calculating 12% of 370,000 for the whole 2019-2022 period, and not for a single year; it is assigned to the final year of the period because the sources consulted give no year-by-year breakdown.

'famílias assentadas' (settled families) and 'títulos entregues' (titles delivered) measure distinct and non-sequential stages of the agrarian reform process — the creation of, or the incorporation of families into, a land settlement project, on one side, and the delivery of the property document to families already settled (often years after the settlement), on the other. The two numbers are neither additive nor directly comparable year by year.

pontos.obs: titles delivered in 2017: floor figure ('more than 26,000'), as reported by INCRA/Agência Brasil; no exact number was found.

titles delivered: figure covering the whole 2019-2022 period (Bolsonaro administration), attributed to the final year of the period because the sources have no year-by-year breakdown; calculated as 12% of the 370 thousand titling documents released by the government, a percentage that specialized reporting indicates corresponds to definitive titles (TD/CDRU), excluding the 88% that are Contratos de Concessão de Uso (CCU, a provisional document).

yanomami.titulo: Deaths recorded in the Terra Indígena Yanomami
yanomami.orgao: Ministério da Saúde / SESAI — DSEI Yanomami
yanomami.serie_codigo: SIASI (Sistema de Informação da Atenção à Saúde Indígena) — consolidação do Centro de Operações de Emergência (COE) Yanomami
yanomami.criterio: absolute number of deaths from all causes, at all ages, recorded by the indigenous health system in the territory of the Terra Indígena Yanomami, by calendar year (January to December)

fonte.nome: Ministério da Saúde / SESAI — dados de óbitos na Terra Indígena Yanomami, consolidados em levantamento enviado ao Congresso Nacional (divulgado em agosto de 2026)

notas.nota: no confirmed annual death totals for the period before 2019 were found in the official sources consulted; 2019 is the first year with a confirmed annual figure.

the count of deaths in the territory depends on the field recording capacity of the indigenous health system — the number of multidisciplinary teams in operation, the number of base hubs and health posts in service, and whether or not active case finding is carried out in the villages. Changes in that capacity over the years affect direct comparison between the annual totals, both in periods of expansion and in periods of reduction of teams and of access to the communities.

bulletins from the Centro de Operações de Emergência (COE) Yanomami released by the Ministério da Saúde in January 2024 and May 2025 reported, at moments before the final consolidation of the records, figures of 428 deaths for 2023 and 337 deaths for 2024. The values adopted in this series (435 and 347, respectively) are those in the most recent survey sent to the Congresso Nacional in August 2026, which reflects the updating of records over time relative to the earlier bulletins.

the 2026 figure refers only to the first half of the year (January to June), marked with type 'projecao' because it is a partial figure; it does not correspond to a full calendar year and is not directly comparable with the annual totals of the other years in the series.

desemprego_pme.titulo: Unemployment rate — PME (Pesquisa Mensal de Emprego)
desemprego_pme.serie_codigo: PME - SIDRA tabela 13 (metodologia antiga, 1998-2002) e SIDRA tabela 2176 (metodologia nova, 2003-2015)
desemprego_pme.criterio: Simple arithmetic mean of the monthly unemployment rates measured by the PME, for the total of the six metropolitan regions surveyed (Recife, Salvador, Belo Horizonte, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo and Porto Alegre) — territorial code 'Total das áreas - PME' in SIDRA. From 1998 to 2002 the old PME series is used ('taxa de desemprego aberto - semana', people aged 15 or over, SIDRA table 13, variable 8); from 2003 to 2015 the new PME series is used ('taxa de desocupação', people aged 10 or over, both sexes, SIDRA table 2176, variable 1031). The two methodologies measure different concepts of unemployment and are NOT comparable with each other — see notes. Calculation verified: the simple average of the 12 months reproduces exactly the official annual figures released by IBGE in the years for which a press release was available (1999, 2000, 2013, 2014), which validates the method for the other years.

fonte.nome: IBGE - Sistema IBGE de Recuperação Automática (SIDRA), tabela 13 (PME, metodologia antiga, série encerrada) e tabela 2176 (PME, metodologia nova, série encerrada)

notas.nota: The IBGE did not release a figure for August 2000 in this series (a collection failure recorded in SIDRA itself). The 2000 average was calculated with the 11 months available, not with the 12 months of the year.

Year of methodological transition: the old PME was discontinued in December 2002 and the new PME began to be released from March 2002, running in parallel for a few months. The 2002 value here uses the OLD series (complete, Brazil/PME total, Jan-Dec). The new series, for the same months of 2002, shows rates of around 11%-13% (almost double), showing that the two methodologies are not comparable.

Series break between 2002 and 2003: from 2003 on the values in this series come from the NEW PME methodology (introduced in 2002), which broadened the concept of unemployment (closer to ILO recommendations), used a new sample base and changed the age cut-off from 15+ to 10+ years. This produces a jump in level (from about 7% to about 12%) that reflects a change in methodology, not a real and abrupt worsening of the labor market. Comparisons between years before and after 2003 should be avoided or should explicitly mention this break.

The PME (new methodology) was discontinued in March 2016, with 2015 as the last full year of data. The survey was replaced by the PNAD Contínua, which has national coverage (all of Brazil, not just 6 metropolitan regions) and a different sample and questionnaire. PME values are NOT comparable with PNAD Contínua values (see series 'desemprego_pnad'), even for years in which the two surveys coexisted (2012-2015).

inss_fila.titulo: INSS backlog — pending claims awaiting review
inss_fila.serie_codigo: Boletim Transparência Previdenciária (MPS) e divulgações oficiais do INSS/MPS
inss_fila.criterio: Stock of benefit applications backlogged at the INSS awaiting review ('the INSS queue'), on the date indicated at each point — it is a measure of STOCK at an instant in time (like a snapshot), not an annual average. That is why there can be more than one point in the same year, and the series is not a continuous annual one: only points with a date and a number officially released by the INSS, by the Ministério da Previdência Social (Transparência Previdenciária bulletin) or by press outlets that explicitly attribute the number to those official sources were included. It was not possible to confirm, with a dated official source, any figure prior to 2023; the series may have existed before that, but no official release with an exact number for 2016-2022 was found in this collection.

fonte.nome: Ministério da Previdência Social / INSS — divulgações do boletim Transparência Previdenciária e balanços de imprensa do INSS (Agência de Notícias/Agência Gov/Agência Brasil e Correio Braziliense, com atribuição explícita a dados oficiais do MPS/INSS)

notas.nota: The INSS queue is not a continuous annual series: it is the stock of pending applications at a given moment, released irregularly (sometimes monthly, sometimes with no release for months). The points here are dated one-off measurements, not annual averages.

Changes in the counting criteria affect the comparison between dates: what counts as the 'queue' may include or exclude, depending on the release, applications that depend on action by the insured person (such as submitting documents), applications held up for more than 45 days, and different benefit categories (initial recognition of entitlement, maintenance, review, appeals, court claims). In July 2023 the government launched a specific program (a Medida Provisória with bonuses for civil servants) to reduce the queue, which may also have changed the way the figure is measured and released over time.

The 24/08/2026 figure is a partial figure for the month (the queue still moving), released as 'the lowest level in the historical series that began in January 2023' by the INSS Benefits director at a meeting of the Conselho Nacional de Previdência Social.

desemprego_pnad.serie_codigo: PNAD Contínua, tabela SIDRA 6381 (série trimestral) e divulgações anuais da Agência IBGE
desemprego_pnad.criterio: Annual average of the unemployment rate for people aged 14 or over, Brazil, calculated by IBGE from the PNAD Contínua microdata (it is not a simple arithmetic mean of the four rounded quarters). For 2012-2020, the figures follow the publication 'PNAD Contínua - Retrospectiva 2012-2020' (IBGE, Jan/2021); the 2014 and 2019 figures were updated to the numbers presented in the more recent publication 'PNAD Contínua - Retrospectiva 2012-2024' (IBGE, 2025), which already incorporates methodological revisions. From 2021 to 2025, the figures come from specific annual releases by the Agência de Notícias do IBGE ('taxa anual/média anual de desocupação'). For 2026, the year has not yet closed; the figure presented is the rate for the most recent rolling quarter available in SIDRA table 6381 (May-June-July/2026), flagged as a partial figure.

fonte.nome: IBGE - PNAD Contínua, SIDRA tabela 6381, e Agência de Notícias IBGE (divulgações anuais de 'taxa anual de desocupação')

notas.nota: The PNAD Contínua series begins in 2012 (first rolling quarter released: Jan-Feb-Mar/2012). It is not comparable with the PME series (see series 'desemprego_pme'), which used a different sample, concept and geographic coverage (only 6 metropolitan regions, against the national coverage of the PNAD Contínua).

IBGE periodically revises the retroactive values of this series, among other reasons because of the update of the population projections used to expand the sample (for example, after the 2022 Censo). This can produce small differences between publications: the 2020 rate appears as 13.5% in the retrospective publication of Jan/2021, but as 13.8% in a comparison cited in a later release (Feb/2022) about the 2021 result. The values from 2012 to 2020 in this series follow, unless otherwise indicated, the retrospective publication of Jan/2021; small divergences of tenths of a percentage point relative to more recent versions are expected and do not indicate a collection error.

The year 2026 is incomplete. The figure shown (5,3%) is the unemployment rate for the rolling quarter May-June-July/2026, the most recent available in SIDRA table 6381 on the collection date (September/2026), and not the annual average rate (which is only calculated after the year closes).

The figures from 2000 to 2005 are DERIVED; they are not the number published directly by IBGE as 'accumulated in the year': table 655, which covers that period, only provides variable 63 ('IPCA - Variação mensal') by group (c315), with no accumulated-in-the-year variable. Each year's accumulated figure was composed from the twelve monthly changes published in table 655 (c315=7170), using the formula accumulated = (∏(1 + monthly_change/100) − 1) × 100, with rounding to two decimal places only in the final result. The composition was validated by reproducing in this same way the years 2006, 2007 and 2008 (months from table 655 for Jan-Jun/2006 and table 2938 for the remainder) and comparing them with the 'accumulated in the year' figures published by IBGE for those three years: the differences were 0.00, -0.02 and +0.01 percentage point, respectively — all within the tolerance of 0.05 p.p., confirming that the composition reproduces the official index.

fonte.nome: IBGE - PNAD Contínua trimestral, SIDRA tabela 4099, variável 4118 ('Taxa composta de subutilização da força de trabalho, na semana de referência, das pessoas de 14 anos ou mais de idade')

subutilizacao.criterio: Composite labor underutilisation rate: it adds together unemployed people, people underemployed due to insufficient hours (they work fewer than 40 hours a week, would like to work more and are available) and the potential labor force (outside the labor force, but willing and available to work). The denominator is the EXPANDED labor force — the labor force plus the potential labor force — and not the labor force used in the unemployment rate. That is why it is always higher: it measures something else, it does not contradict the other one. Figure for the 4th quarter of each year.

notas.nota: Definition of a discouraged worker (desalento), according to the IBGE: a person outside the labor force (not employed and not classified as unemployed) who would like to work and would be available to take a job in the reference week, but took no effective step to look for work in the previous 30 days because of a belief that no suitable available job would be found (for example: there is no work in the locality, the person lacks experience or qualifications, or there is no work suited to that person's circumstances). Discouraged workers are a subset of the potential labor force.

The year 2026 is incomplete. The figures presented (composite labor underutilisation rate: 12,9%; percentage of discouraged workers: 2,1%) refer to the 2nd quarter of 2026 (April-May-June), the most recent available in SIDRA tables 4099 and 6813 on the date of collection (September/2026) — not to the 4th quarter, used in the other years of this series, and not to a closed annual average. Flagged as a partial figure.

On 31/07/2025 the IBGE rebased the entire PNAD Contínua series using the population projections that incorporate the Censo 2022, which found a smaller population than the earlier projections assumed. The percentage RATES were recalculated for the whole series and remain comparable with one another; the ABSOLUTE NUMBERS in millions of people published before and after the rebasing are not directly comparable. Source: Agência IBGE, 15/08/2025.

notas.nota: All 27 values for each quarter were collected directly from the SIDRA API (table 4099, variable 4099, level N3), in requests made in September 2026.

IBGE rebased the PNAD Contínua historical series on 31/07/2025, on the basis of the population totals of the Projeções de População released in 2024, which incorporate the results of the 2022 Demographic Census. According to an Agência IBGE news item of 15/08/2025 about the 2nd quarter of 2025: 'The data include the rebasing of the PNAD Contínua historical series, already released this past 31/7'. The news item does not detail exactly which retroactive quarters were recalculated, only that the rebasing reached the historical series. Source: https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/agencia-noticias/2012-agencia-de-noticias/noticias/44246-desocupacao-recua-em-18-unidades-da-federacao-no-segundo-trimestre-de-2025 . The collection of this series (SIDRA table 4099) was made in September 2026, so the figures here already reflect that rebasing.
This series should not be used to compare states with each other or to attribute causality to state governments; it measures only the unemployment rate measured by the PNAD Contínua.

pontos.obs: 2nd quarter of 2026 (Apr-May-Jun), the most recent quarter available in SIDRA table 4099 on the collection date (Sep 2026); it is neither the 4th quarter nor an annual average.

homicidios_uf.orgao: Ipea / Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública (FBSP)
homicidios_uf.criterio: Rate of 'homicides' by state (UF), defined by the Atlas da Violência as the sum of deaths by assault (ICD-10 X85-Y09) and deaths by legal intervention (ICD-10 Y35-Y36), recorded in the Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (SIM/Ministério da Saúde) by the victim's municipality/UF of residence, divided by the population estimated by IBGE for the UF, per 100,000 inhabitants. Same definition of 'homicides' used in the national series (homicidios.json); it differs from the 'Mortes Violentas Intencionais' (MVI) metric of the Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública/FBSP, measured from state police records.

fonte.nome: Ipea/FBSP — Atlas da Violência 2016 (Nota Técnica nº 17, tabela 1.2, para os anos 2004-2013) e Atlas da Violência 2026 (tabela 2.1, para os anos 2014-2024)

notas.nota: Public security is mainly a state responsibility (and, to a lesser extent, municipal and federal) in Brazil; levels and variations in the homicide rate across UFs reflect, among other factors, differences in the demographic, socioeconomic and territorial structure of each state, and do not, on their own, allow public policy to be assessed or a cause to be assigned.

Changes over time, and differences between states, in the quality of the completion of cause of death on SIM death certificates — in particular in the share of violent deaths recorded with an undetermined cause (ICD-10 chapter XX, category 'events of undetermined intent', Y10-Y34) — affect the comparability of homicide rates between states and between years: a state or period with greater underreporting/misclassification of cause tends to understate the corresponding homicide rate relative to others.

The Atlas da Violência periodically revises the entire historical series with each new edition (among other reasons, because of updates to the IBGE population projections, including after the Censo 2022, and updates to SIM records). For that reason, the same year may appear with different rates depending on the edition consulted; see the 2014 note below for a concrete example by UF.

Each edition of the Atlas da Violência publishes, in the tables by state (UF), only a window of roughly the 11 most recent years (e.g., the 2016 edition published 2004-2014; the 2026 edition published 2014-2024). No table by UF from the Atlas da Violência covering years before 2004 was found within the time frame of this data collection (September 2026). The years 2004 to 2013 in this series come from the 2016 edition of the Atlas (Nota Técnica nº 17, table 1.2), because no more recent edition republishing those years specifically by UF was found; therefore, unlike 2014-2024, those years were not updated by revisions in later editions of the Atlas.

Transition year between the two source tables used in this series. The 2016 edition of the Atlas (table 1.2) published for 2014, for example, SP=13,4 and RR=32,0 per 100,000; the 2026 edition (table 2.1, the most recent) publishes for that same year of 2014 the revised values SP=14,1 and RR=34,3. In this series we chose to use, for 2014, the value from the most recent edition (2026), following the same logic adopted in the national series homicidios.json; the 2016 edition values for 2014 are not shown here.

The 2023 values in this table by UF come from the 2026 edition of the Atlas da Violência (table 2.1) and not from the 2025 edition (table 2.1, 2013-2023 base): the two editions published different numbers for 2023 in practically every UF (e.g.: Amapá appears as 57,4 in the 2025 edition and as 65,3 in the 2026 edition; São Paulo appears as 6,4 in the 2025 edition and as 6,6 in the 2026 edition). This is consistent with the note on periodic revision of the series and does not indicate a collection error.
2024 is the last year with a homicide rate by state published by the Atlas da Violência up to the date of this collection (September 2026), in the 2026 edition (released in May 2026).

carga_tributaria.orgao: Receita Federal do Brasil (RFB) - Centro de Estudos Tributários e Aduaneiros
carga_tributaria.serie_codigo: Carga Tributária no Brasil (relatórios anuais, várias edições 1998-2024)
carga_tributaria.criterio: Receita Federal do Brasil (RFB): ratio between total tax revenue (taxes and contributions under federal, state and municipal jurisdiction, measured on a cash basis) and GDP for the year. From the edition of the report referring to base year 2024 (published in December/2025), the RFB began to exclude from the calculation FGTS deposits and contributions to the 'Sistema S', aligning the methodology with the IMF's Government Finance Statistics Manual 2014 and the OECD's Revenue Statistics. The points from 2015 to 2024 of this series already reflect this new methodology (recalculated by the RFB itself in the 2024 report); the points from 1998 to 2014 follow the previous methodology (which included FGTS and Sistema S) and are NOT directly comparable to those from 2015 onwards. See notes.

fonte.nome: Receita Federal do Brasil - Estudos Tributários e Aduaneiros, série 'Carga Tributária no Brasil'

relatorios_utilizados.obs: consultado para checagem cruzada de 1999-2002; valores substituídos pela edição 2003, mais recente
consultado para checagem cruzada de 2002-2006; valores substituídos pela edição 2007, mais recente, para 2003-2006

relatorios_utilizados.edicao: Carga Tributária no Brasil - 2024 (Tabela 06, metodologia nova - exclui FGTS e Sistema S)

notas.nota: The Receita Federal do Brasil (RFB) and IBGE (Sistema de Contas Nacionais) calculate the gross tax burden with different criteria: the RFB uses a cash basis (amounts actually collected) applied to the collection of taxes and contributions, while IBGE uses the accrual concept of the 'general government' institutional sector of the National Accounts. The two bodies arrive at different figures for the same year. This series uses exclusively the RFB criterion (the source that the Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional itself identifies as responsible for publishing Brazil's official tax burden figure).

Values for years before 2003 underwent significant revisions in later editions of the report, attributable above all to the changes of GDP base made by IBGE (the 2007 rebasing, with 2000 as reference, and the 2015 rebasing, with 2010 as reference), which retroactively change all %GDP ratios. In this series, for each year the most recent value available in some edition of the RFB report consulted is used; for 1998-2002 no revision was found in an edition later than that of 2003, so the values for those years may not fully reflect the 2007 rebasing.

The 2007 figure measured at the time by the report 'Carga Tributária no Brasil 2007' (published in Dec/2008) was 34,79% of GDP, reported at the time as a record for the series. The figure of 33,66% used here comes from the 2016 edition of the report (Table TRIB 01-B), which is more recent and already reflects the 2015 GDP rebasing; the RFB's own 2018 report again cites 2007 as the year with the highest tax burden of the decade, at 33,64%.

Starting with the report covering 2024 (published in December 2025), the RFB began excluding FGTS and Sistema S from the calculation of the gross tax burden, which the Receita Federal itself describes as 'an important inflection in the historical series' that affects figures used for decades by public institutions, market analysts and academia. That change was applied retroactively by the RFB only to the 2015-2024 series (Table 06 of the 2024 report). The values from 1998 to 2014 in this series follow the earlier methodology (which includes FGTS and Sistema S) and are not directly comparable to the values from 2015 on.

2024 is the last year covered by an official Receita Federal report available at the collection date (September/2026); the report referring to 2024 was published in December/2025. The Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (STN) has published since 2019 a complementary and unofficial estimate of the 'gross tax burden of general government', with a similar methodology (GFSM 2014/IMF, also excluding FGTS and Sistema S since the 2024 revision); according to the STN this estimate reached 32.32% of GDP in 2024 (note of March/2025, later revised to 32.22%) and 32.40% of GDP in 2025 (note of April/2026). Since the STN is not, by the STN's own definition, the body responsible for publishing the official figure, the 2025 point was not included in this series; it appears only in this note.

educacao_pnad.titulo: Illiteracy and schooling — PNAD and PNAD Contínua
educacao_pnad.unidade: % (illiteracy and share with 12+ years of schooling) or years (mean years of schooling) — see the definition of each category in "criterio"
educacao_pnad.orgao: IBGE — Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística
educacao_pnad.serie_codigo: PNAD (pesquisa anual, série encerrada) e PNAD Contínua Anual (módulo Educação, 2º trimestre) — tabelas SIDRA 1187 (alfabetização 15+, PNAD), 1189 (anos de estudo 25+, PNAD), 7113 (analfabetismo 15+, PNAD Contínua) e 7133 (grupos de anos de estudo 25+, PNAD Contínua)
categorias: Illiteracy rate, aged 15 or over — PNAD (%)
Illiteracy rate, aged 15 or over — PNAD Contínua (%)
Mean years of schooling, aged 25 or over — PNAD (years)
People aged 25 or over with 12 or more years of schooling — PNAD Contínua (%)
educacao_pnad.criterio: Brazil, both sexes, total population (not only employed persons). (1) and (2) 'Illiteracy rate' = percentage of people aged 15 or over who declare themselves unable to read and write a simple note (does not include functional illiteracy). Category (1) 'PNAD' is the arithmetic complement (100% − literacy rate) of the 'Taxa de alfabetização das pessoas de 15 anos ou mais de idade' published by IBGE in SIDRA table 1187 (no SIDRA table publishing the illiteracy rate directly, rather than the literacy rate, for the old PNAD was located within the collection period); category (2) 'PNAD Contínua' is published directly as the 'illiteracy rate' in SIDRA table 7113. (3) 'Average years of schooling of people aged 25 or over', in years, published directly by SIDRA table 1189 (old PNAD, series discontinued in 2009). (4) PNAD Contínua no longer publishes, on a continuous basis, a SIDRA table with the average years of schooling or with the exact percentage of people aged 25 or over with 'completed secondary education'; the closest continuous indicator available in SIDRA table 7133 is the percentage of people aged 25 or over who fall into the group '12 years or more of schooling' (which includes those who completed secondary education and also those who went beyond it) — this is why category (4) uses that percentage as a proxy, and it is not directly comparable to the figure in years of category (3).

fonte.nome: IBGE — SIDRA, tabelas 1187 e 1189 (PNAD) e 7113 e 7133 (PNAD Contínua Anual)

notas.nota: SIDRA table 1189 (average years of schooling, PNAD) is available for 1992-2009, but does not include 1994 or 2000: there was no PNAD in those two years (1994 because of budget restrictions and 2000 because it was a Censo Demográfico year). Series (3) of this collection begins in 1998 only because that is the first year the Enem was administered, not because of a limitation of the source — the years 1992, 1993, 1995, 1996 and 1997 are also available in SIDRA table 1189 but were not included here.

Category (1) 'Illiteracy rate — PNAD' begins in 2004 because that is the first year available in SIDRA table 1187 ('Literacy rate of persons aged 15 and over by sex'); no equivalent SIDRA table with 1998-2003 coverage was located within the collection time frame (September 2026). Series 1187 also does not include 2010 (a Censo Demográfico year, with no PNAD).

Category (3) 'Average years of schooling — PNAD' (SIDRA table 1189) is a series discontinued by IBGE in 2009 (last reference year); the annual PNAD was replaced by the PNAD Contínua from 2012 on (there was an interruption in 2010-2011 because of the 2010 Censo Demográfico). The PNAD Contínua did not resume publishing 'average years of schooling' for people aged 25 or over as a continuous SIDRA table — which is why there are no points in this category between 2010 and 2026. Category (4) of this series covers part of that period (2016 on) with a different indicator (see 'criterio').

The PNAD Contínua begins in 2012 (first moving quarter released: Jan-Feb-Mar/2012), but the annual Education module (2nd quarter), from which the SIDRA tables 7113 and 7133 used here come, is only available from 2016 on in those tables specifically; no equivalent SIDRA table (same age range and same definition) published for 2012-2015 was found within the data collection time frame. PNAD (the old one) and PNAD Contínua are different surveys — sample, questionnaire and weighting methodology are not the same — which is why they appear here as separate categories, never spliced into a single series line.

SIDRA tables 7113 and 7133 (PNAD Contínua Anual, Education module) have no data published for 2020 and 2021 (the survey jumped straight from 2019 to 2022 in those tables, in the query made in September 2026). It was not possible to confirm, within the collection time frame, the exact reason for this gap, nor to locate an alternative table that fills it; for that reason 2020 and 2021 are absent from categories (2) and (4) of this series.

Data collected in September 2026. The year 2026 has not closed yet and the PNAD Contínua Educação is an annual survey (released once a year, with data from the 2nd quarter); the most recent edition available in SIDRA tables 7113 and 7133 on the date of collection is the 2025 one (released on June 19, 2026). The values in this series may be revised by IBGE in future releases, including retroactively (for example, after updates to population projections resulting from the 2022 Censo); the figures here reflect what was published in SIDRA at the time of collection.

pib_mundo.criterio: Annual real change in world GDP, aggregated by the World Bank from national GDPs converted to constant 2015 prices in dollars and added together. It is an aggregate weighted by the size of the economies: the result of the large economies weighs more than that of the small ones. It is not a simple average across countries.

fonte.nome: Banco Mundial — World Development Indicators

notas.nota: the World Bank series runs to 2024 as of the collection date (September 2026); 2025 and 2026 do not yet have a measured figure published in that database, which is why the world line ends before the Brazil bars. No projection was added.
the world aggregate is revised when countries revise their own national accounts; values for earlier years may change from one edition of the database to another.

divida_antiga.criterio: Gross general government debt measured by the criterion the Banco Central used before the 2008 methodological revision, in December of each year. It is a DIFFERENT yardstick from the current series: in the years in which both exist, they give different numbers for the same month. That is why they appear as separate lines and are never spliced.

fonte.nome: Banco Central — Sistema Gerenciador de Séries Temporais

notas.nota: this series begins in January 2002 in the Banco Central database; there is no value earlier than that date under this criterion.

in December 2006, the same month appears as 45,29% by this criterion and as 55,48% by the current methodology. The difference is one of definition — mainly the treatment of repo operations and of the securities in the Banco Central's portfolio — and not a data revision.

divida_liquida.criterio: Net debt of the consolidated public sector in December of each year: gross debt MINUS public sector credits (international reserves, credits with public banks and other assets). It measures something different from gross debt and is systematically smaller — it is not a corrected version of it.

fonte.nome: Banco Central — Sistema Gerenciador de Séries Temporais

notas.nota: this series begins in December 2001 in the Banco Central database. The Banco Central's monthly fiscal statistics, in all public versions, do not go back beyond that date — that is why no line in this chart reaches 1998.
the 2026 value is the most recent month published (July 2026), not the December close.

pix_transacoes.criterio: total number of Pix transactions (payments, transfers and withdrawals/cash back) settled over each calendar year, as compiled by the Banco Central for the Relatório de Gestão do Pix.

fonte.nome: Banco Central do Brasil — Relatório de Gestão do Pix 2023-2025

notas.nota: Pix began operating in November 2020 (Resolução BCB nº 1, of 12/8/2020, created the arrangement; transactions started on 16/11/2020 for individuals according to the BCB schedule), which is why the 2020 figure corresponds to less than two months of operation.

The 2025 figure is the consolidated annual value published in the Relatório de Gestão do Pix 2023-2025, released by the Banco Central; it was not possible to confirm, within the timeframe of this collection (September 2026), whether the figure is final or subject to later revision.

There is no Pix series before November 2020, and it is not a gap in the collection: the arrangement did not exist. For anyone wanting the long comparison, the instrument Pix actually replaced is the cheque, and the Central Bank has published that count since the 1990s — from about 2.5 billion cheques in 1999 to 109 million in 2020. That series is not in this chart because it has a definition break in 2016, when the statistics began including operations within the same bank, and it would deserve a chart of its own with the break marked.

pix_usuarios.unidade: millions of users (individuals and businesses with at least one Pix key)
pix_usuarios.criterio: number of users (individuals and legal entities) with at least one Pix key registered in the Diretório de Identificadores de Contas Transacionais (DICT), by year, according to the Banco Central.

fonte.nome: Banco Central do Brasil — Relatório de Gestão do Pix 2023-2025

tempo_abertura_empresa.titulo: Average time to open a business registered with Juntas Comerciais
tempo_abertura_empresa.unidade: hours (value of the last four-month period published in each year)
tempo_abertura_empresa.orgao: Ministério do Empreendedorismo, da Microempresa e da Empresa de Pequeno Porte (ex-MDIC) — Mapa de Empresas
tempo_abertura_empresa.criterio: average time, in hours, between the viability stage (confirmation by the municipality and by the Junta Comercial that the company may establish itself at the address and use the chosen name) and the registration stage (filing of the articles of incorporation by the Junta Comercial), for companies registered at Juntas Comerciais whose relevant bodies are integrated into the Rede Nacional para Simplificação do Registro e da Legalização de Empresas e Negócios (Redesim). It does not cover the MEI, does not include the time spent by the citizen between stages, and does not count the issuance of permits/licenses. The Mapa de Empresas bulletins are published every four months, not annually: there is no 'value for the year'. Each point in this series is the last four-month period published in that year, and which period was used is written at each point. Up to 2022 the bulletins report in 'days and hours' and from 2023 on in hours; the metric is the same and everything has been converted to hours here.

fonte.nome: Ministério do Empreendedorismo, da Microempresa e da Empresa de Pequeno Porte — Mapa de Empresas, boletins quadrimestrais

notas.nota: Method break in 2021: Law no. 14,195 of 26 August 2021 waived the viability stage in certain cases — exclusively digital activity, or a municipality that does not answer in time. That reduces the measured time without the real process having shrunk in the same proportion. Comparing 2020 with 2022 onwards mixes two definitions of what 'opening a company' is.

The series is not only a fall. Its best value is 2024, at 18 hours; after that the time rises again — 21 hours in 2025 and 23 hours in July 2026. A chart that stopped at 2024 would tell a different story from the one the data tells.

The indicator excludes the MEI, which today accounts for most businesses opened in Brazil, and covers only municipalities integrated into Redesim — and that integration grew over the period, so the composition of the sample changes from year to year.

estatais_lucro.titulo: Aggregate net profit of federal state-owned companies
estatais_lucro.orgao: Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos (MGI) — e, até 2019, Ministério do Planejamento/Ministério da Economia
estatais_lucro.serie_codigo: Boletim das Empresas Estatais Federais (até 4º tri/2022) e Relatório Agregado das Empresas Estatais Federais (a partir do ano-base 2023)
estatais_lucro.criterio: sum of the annual net profit (or loss), after taxes, of the federal state-owned companies under direct control of the Union classified as not dependent on the Tesouro Nacional (public companies and mixed-capital companies, e.g.: Petrobras, Banco do Brasil, BNDES, Caixa Econômica Federal, Correios, Eletrobras up to its privatization in 2022, among others) — 44 companies in the 2023-2025 base, according to the most recent reports. Values in current R$ of each year, with no inflation adjustment. This measure is NOT comparable to the Banco Central's primary balance (series estatais_primario), which uses a smaller universe of companies and a different fiscal concept.

fonte.nome: MGI — Relatório Agregado das Empresas Estatais Federais 2026 (ano-base 2025)

notas.nota: Figure (a loss of R$ 32 billion) taken from a news report (Revista Oeste, based on official government data) that cites the aggregate result of the federal state-owned companies in 2015; it was not possible to locate the original official bulletin for that year in the current collection, so the number does not have the same precision (decimal places) as the years with a source in an official bulletin. URL: https://revistaoeste.com/economia/do-prejuizo-ao-lucro-a-reviravolta-nas-contas-das-empresas-estatais/

The figure of R$ 28,334 billion refers to the aggregate net profit of the 'federal state-owned companies not dependent on the Tesouro Nacional', released by the then Ministério do Planejamento in March 2018. Source: https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/geral/noticia/2018-03/lucro-das-estatais-cresce-214-em-2017-diz-planejamento

The values from 2018 to 2022 (71.992 / 111.062 / 61.202 / 186.046 / 273.597 R$ billions) come from the table with the historical series of consolidated 'Resultado Líquido' published in the Boletim das Estatais for the 4th quarter of 2022 (MGI). According to the same bulletin, five groups (Petrobras, Banco do Brasil, BNDES, Caixa and Eletrobras) accounted for about 96% of total assets and for most of the aggregate profit in that period — see the series estatais_empresas for the figures by group.

From 2023 onwards, the federal government stopped publishing the quarterly Boletim das Estatais with the company-by-company breakdown that existed up to 2022, and began publishing an annual Relatório Agregado (base year). The 2023 figure (R$ 197.9 billion, down 28% on 2022) was obtained from a news report citing the official report, since the PDF of the 'base year 2023' report could not be accessed directly in this collection (the official URL returned the gov.br institutional page instead of the file). estatais_primario.titulo: Primary balance of federal state-owned companies
estatais_primario.unidade: % of GDP (12-month cumulative flow, December position of each year)
estatais_primario.orgao: Banco Central do Brasil — Necessidades de Financiamento do Setor Público (NFSP)
estatais_primario.criterio: primary balance (revenue minus non-financial expenditure, not including interest) of the federal state-owned companies, measured by the Banco Central in the public-sector fiscal statistics (NFSP), excluding exchange-rate devaluation, as a 12-month cumulative flow; the December figure of each year corresponds to the result for the calendar year. IMPORTANT — a different universe from the estatais_lucro series: from 2009 onwards this Banco Central methodology EXCLUDES Petrobras, and from 2010 onwards it excludes Eletrobras; moreover, this series NEVER includes the federal public banks (Banco do Brasil, Caixa Econômica Federal, BNDES), which are classified as financial institutions and do not enter the NFSP statistics for non-financial state-owned companies. Because it covers a smaller set of companies and a different concept of result (cash/fiscal, without interest, excluding accounting items such as changes in net worth and financial results), this series must not be added to or compared directly with the aggregate accounting net profit (estatais_lucro series).

fonte.nome: Banco Central do Brasil — Sistema Gerenciador de Séries Temporais (SGS), série 5790 — NFSP sem desvalorização cambial (% PIB), fluxo acumulado em 12 meses, resultado primário, empresas estatais federais

notas.nota: The Banco Central's SGS 5790 series begins in November 2002. This series contains no official BCB figures for the primary balance of federal state-owned companies in 1998-2001.
From 2009 onward, the Banco Central methodology for the primary balance of federal state-owned companies excluded Petrobras from the calculation.
From 2010 onward, the Banco Central methodology also excluded Eletrobras from the calculation (in addition to Petrobras, already excluded since 2009).
The 2026 figure refers to the flow accumulated over 12 months to July/2026 (the last month available in the series on the collection date, September 2026), not the December/2026 close.

pontos.obs: first year in which the BCB methodology excludes Petrobras from the calculation
first year in which the BCB methodology also excludes Eletrobras from the calculation
partial figure: 12-month cumulative flow through July 2026, not the December close

estatais_empresas.titulo: Annual net result by federal state-owned company
estatais_empresas.orgao: Diversas — ver fonte por ponto (empresas, MGI/Boletim das Estatais, imprensa especializada)
estatais_empresas.serie_codigo: sem código único — série composta a partir de balanços das empresas e do Boletim das Estatais/Relatório Agregado do MGI
estatais_empresas.criterio: annual net profit or loss (after taxes), in nominal R$ of each year, for each company/economic group. For Petrobras, Banco do Brasil, BNDES and Caixa in the years 2018 to 2022, the figure is that of the consolidated 'economic group' (Grupo Petrobras, Grupo BB, Grupo BNDES, Grupo Caixa), per the table in the MGI Boletim das Estatais (fourth quarter of 2022) — this scope may differ slightly from the standalone parent-company result reported by the company itself. For the remaining years, the figure is the net profit reported by the company itself in the corresponding balance sheet/earnings release (Petrobras: the company's result; Banco do Brasil, BNDES and Caixa: when the institution reports 'accounting/statutory net profit' and 'adjusted/recurring profit' separately, the 'obs' field of each data point indicates which of the two was used, since the accounting figure was not located for every year). Correios: annual accounting net loss/profit of Empresa Brasileira de Correios e Telégrafos. For the years before 2018 the basis changes from company to company, and that is stated at each point: Banco do Brasil enters under consolidated IFRS via item 3.1 of the Reference Forms filed with the CVM (2009-2017); BNDES enters as the institution, not as the BNDES System nor as an economic group (2001-2016); Correios enter via net income for the year in their own financial statements (2002-2012). None of those bases is identical to the 'economic group' basis of the Boletim das Estatais used from 2018 to 2022 — in 2018, for instance, BB appears with R$ 12.9 billion on the group basis and R$ 15.1 billion under IFRS. The correct reading of the line is therefore each company's trend, not the difference from one year to the next around 2017-2018.

fonte.nome: Composta: balanços/releases de resultados de cada empresa, Boletim das Estatais (MGI) e Relatório Agregado das Empresas Estatais Federais (MGI); ver 'obs' de cada ponto para a fonte específica

notas.nota: These are each year's current values, with no inflation adjustment. Comparing 2003 with 2024 in nominal reais overstates the recent years: accumulated IPCA inflation alone multiplies prices by more than four over the period. The series is for seeing how each company behaved over time, and the relative order of magnitude between them in the same year — not for saying that one government made X times the profit of another.

Caixa Econômica Federal still has no figures before 2018. Caixa's financial statements are public and their address is known — caixa.gov.br, financial information section — but the domain blocks automated reading and this site's collection could not open them. The figures circulating in the press were not used, because the rule here is an exact figure with a source document. The gap is in the collection, not in the source.

Petrobras has no figures between 2006 and 2011, nor between 2000 and 2004, in this collection; coverage by company is uneven because it prioritises sources with an exact figure and a URL over estimates.

The figures for Petrobras, Banco do Brasil, BNDES and Caixa in 2018-2022 are for the 'economic group' (Table of the Boletim das Estatais 4T/2022, MGI), not for the company on its own. Source: https://www.gov.br/gestao/pt-br/central-de-conteudo/publicacoes/boletins/boletim-das-empresas-estatais-federais/arquivos/boletim-das-estatais-4t-2022.pdf

Eletrobras is not among the categories of this series (the request covered Petrobras, Banco do Brasil, Caixa, BNDES and Correios), but note that the Boletim das Estatais table shows 'Grupo Eletrobrás' with a zero result in 2022 because the company's privatization was completed that year.

The figures for Banco do Brasil (R$ 33,8 billion), BNDES (R$ 21,9 billion) and Caixa (R$ 11,7 billion) in 2023 come from a news report citing the Relatório Agregado das Empresas Estatais Federais 2024 (base year 2023); the official PDF of the report could not be accessed directly in this collection. Source: https://bpmoney.com.br/economia/estatais-brasileiras-lucraram-r-1979-bi-em-2023-queda-de-28/

For 2025, the Banco do Brasil figure (R$ 20.685 bn) is the 'adjusted net profit' released by the bank itself (source: https://cgn.inf.br/noticia/2040057/banco-do-brasil-tem-lucro-de-r-2068-bilhoes-em-2025), not necessarily comparable to the accounting/group criterion used in 2018-2022. For BNDES in 2025 (R$ 15.2 bn), only the 'recurring profit' released by the bank was located (source: https://agenciadenoticias.bndes.gov.br/bndes/BNDES-tem-lucro-recorrente-de-R$-152-bi-em-2025-o-maior-da-historia/); in earlier years (e.g. 2022) BNDES had an accounting profit far above the recurring one because of gains on equity holdings marked to market (e.g. Petrobras and Vale shares), so the 2025 figure may understate the total accounting result. For Caixa in 2025 (R$ 16.051 bn), the figure is the 'accounting net profit', released as such by the institution itself (source: https://spbancarios.com.br/03/2026/lucro-da-caixa-sobe-187-em-2025-e-empregados-exigem-respostas-para-reivindicacoes).

Serpro, Embrapa, EBC and Infraero appear in a series of their own, built from the financial statements published by each company — the quarterly Boletim of the SEST, the source for the first five, aggregates by economic group and has no line for smaller state-owned companies.

Infraero: 2023 is a series break. The 15 airports transferred in the 7th round of concessions — Congonhas among them — accounted for R$ 617,2 million of that year's operating profit, and left the company in 2023. Comparing 2024 and 2025 with the earlier years measures a change of perimeter, not performance. The company today operates 28 regional airports.

Infraero: 2021 and 2022 have no value because the official PDFs for those two financial years are on the company's transparency portal but the server refused access in the attempts made for this collection. The gap is one of access, not of the data not existing.

EBC: the company restates its results frequently, and the difference is large. 2024 came out as a loss of R$ 16,6 million in that year's own financial statements and was restated as R$ 42,2 million in the 2025 comparative figures; 2023 came out as a profit of R$ 34,9 million and was restated as R$ 32,7 million. This series always uses the most recent restated version.
