marcos.numero_ato: Lei nº 15.504, de 15 de setembro de 2026
marcos.nome: Redata — regime especial de tributação para data centers
marcos.o_que_mudou: The law adds arts. 11-A to 11-J to Law no. 11.196/2005 and creates the Special Tax Regime for Datacenter Services. For companies approved by the Federal Revenue Service, it suspends PIS/Pasep, Cofins, IPI and the Import Tax on electronic components and technology products destined for the data centre's fixed assets, both on domestic purchases and on imports; the suspension becomes a zero rate once the company meets its commitments and books the asset. In exchange, art. 11-B requires, cumulatively: allocating at least 10% of the processing and storage supplied to the domestic market; meeting sustainability criteria to be set by regulation; supplying 100% of electricity from renewable or low-emission sources; keeping water efficiency at or below 0.05 litres per kWh; and investing 2% of the value of the equipment in research and development, of which at least 40% in the North, Northeast and Centre-West regions. Projects in those regions have the domestic-market and R&D commitments reduced by 20%. Two points change the real size of the benefit and were barely reported: the list of goods covered depends on an Executive act not yet issued, and the sole paragraph of art. 11-J ends the PIS/Pasep, Cofins and IPI part on 31 December 2026, because of the tax-reform transition — from 2027 on, essentially only the Import Tax remains. The revenue forgone estimated by the government itself is R$ 5.2 billion in 2026, R$ 1.0 billion in 2027 and R$ 1.05 billion in 2028; the R$ 7.2 billion total that circulated is the sum of the three years made by the press, not an official figure. The same law, in a provision unrelated to data centres, channels to the National Fund for Children and Adolescents, for five years, the fines set out in the Digital Statute of the Child and Adolescent.
marcos.autoria: Origem no Poder Executivo: o conteúdo veio da Medida Provisória nº 1.318, de 17 de setembro de 2025, com exposição de motivos assinada por Geraldo Alckmin, Fernando Haddad e Alexandre Silveira. A medida caducou sem votação e a matéria foi reapresentada como Projeto de Lei nº 278/2026, assinado pelo líder do governo na Câmara, deputado José Guimarães (PT-CE) — formalmente autoria parlamentar, materialmente do Executivo. Relator na Câmara: deputado Aguinaldo Ribeiro (PP-PB), com aprovação em Plenário em 24 de fevereiro de 2026. Relator no Senado: senador Cid Gomes (CE), com aprovação em 1º de setembro de 2026, apenas com emendas de redação — por isso o texto não voltou à Câmara. Sancionada integralmente por Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, sem vetos, e publicada em edição extra do Diário Oficial no mesmo dia. Entre os ajustes de redação do Senado está a troca de ‘energia limpa’ por ‘de baixa emissão’, que analistas do setor leram como abertura para o gás natural. Durante a tramitação, entidades reunidas na Coalizão Direitos na Rede, com Idec e Lapin, manifestaram-se contra o regime, alegando concessão de benefício antes de regulação do setor, impacto de energia e água e contrapartidas insuficientes; o governo e os relatores defenderam o regime com o argumento de que cerca de 60% das cargas digitais brasileiras são processadas no exterior e de que operar no Brasil custa cerca de 30% mais, sobretudo pela tributação de equipamentos.

fiscal.por: Suspends PIS/Pasep, Cofins, their import versions, IPI and import duty on purchases of technology goods for data centres, converting them to a zero rate once the commitments are met, for five years. It is a tax break created by this law, and among the provisions I could check there is no estimate of its value and no offsetting measure.

investimento.por: Makes the benefit conditional on investing 2% of the value acquired in research with scientific institutions, teaching bodies or state-owned companies, channels at least 40% of those funds to the North, North-East and Centre-West, and sets a fixed five-year term for the regime.

acesso.disp: Law 11,196: art. 11-B, § 1, I, III and IV and § 10
acesso.por: Requires at least 10% of data processing, storage and handling to be made available to the domestic market, all energy demand to be met from renewable or low-emission sources and a water efficiency index of up to 0.05 litres per kWh to be maintained, with annual measurement.

concorrencia.por: Creates qualification and co-qualification by the Receita Federal, requires tax compliance, bars companies under the Simples Nacional, cuts by 20% the commitments of projects in the North, North-East and Centre-West, and provides for cancellation with a two-year wait before requalifying.

seguranca_juridica.por: Qualification is decided by the Receita Federal with no statutory deadline, central parts were left to later regulation, and non-compliance suspends the benefit with 180 days to put it right. Among the provisions checked there is no transition rule and no protection of vested rights.

expressao.por: Amends Law 15,211/2025 only to channel the fines it provides for to the Fundo Nacional para a Criança e o Adolescente, without defining who restricts content, on what basis or by what procedure.

marcos.numero_ato: Emenda Constitucional nº 72, de 2 de abril de 2013
marcos.nome: Direitos dos trabalhadores domésticos — 1 de 3: a equiparação na Constituição
marcos.serie_item: equal rights written into the Constitution
marcos.o_que_mudou: The amendment rewrote the sole paragraph of art. 7 of the Constitution and extended to domestic workers rights that until then belonged to other urban and rural workers. Eighteen items took effect immediately — among them an 8-hour day and 44-hour week, overtime of at least 50%, paid weekly rest, a night-shift premium, health and safety rules and recognition of collective agreements. Seven others were made conditional on a later law: protection against arbitrary dismissal, unemployment insurance, the FGTS severance fund, the family allowance, childcare and workplace accident insurance. That is why saying 'the domestic workers' amendment guaranteed the FGTS in 2013' is imprecise: it guaranteed it conditional on regulation, which only came in 2015 (item 2 of the sequence).
marcos.autoria: Emenda constitucional não é sancionada nem vetada pelo presidente: é promulgada pelas Mesas da Câmara e do Senado, na forma do art. 60, § 3º da Constituição. Quem assinou foram o deputado Henrique Eduardo Alves e o senador Renan Calheiros, presidentes das duas Casas. Dilma Rousseff era presidenta na data e esteve na cerimônia, mas não assinou o ato — dizer que ela sancionou a emenda é erro. A origem é a PEC nº 478/2010, apresentada em 14 de abril de 2010, ainda no governo Lula, pelo deputado Carlos Bezerra (PMDB-MT); relatoria de Benedita da Silva (PT-RJ) na Comissão Especial da Câmara e de Lídice da Mata (PSB-BA) no Senado. Aprovada na Câmara em 21/11 e 04/12/2012 e no Senado em 19 e 26/03/2013.

seguranca_juridica.disp: sole paragraph of art. 7 of the Constitution, as newly worded
seguranca_juridica.por: Replaces the previous wording, which gave domestic workers a far shorter list of rights, and splits the rights between those of immediate effect and those that depend on a statute — which defines exactly what became enforceable on 3 April 2013 and what arrived only two years later.

fiscal.disp: sole paragraph of art. 7 of the Constitution, as newly worded
fiscal.por: Provides for domestic workers to be integrated into social security and requires this to be done with compliance with tax obligations, principal and ancillary, simplified. It creates social-security spending and shapes the model for collecting from the household employer.

concorrencia.disp: sole paragraph of art. 7 of the Constitution, as newly worded
concorrencia.por: The requirement to simplify compliance with tax obligations is a compliance cost designed for the size of the employer — a household, not a company.

marcos.numero_ato: Lei Complementar nº 150, de 1º de junho de 2015
marcos.nome: Direitos dos trabalhadores domésticos — 2 de 3: a regulamentação que tornou os direitos exigíveis
marcos.serie_item: the regulation that made the rights enforceable
marcos.o_que_mudou: The law regulated the seven items that Amendment 72 (item 1 of the sequence) had left dependent on legislation. It defined the domestic worker as someone working more than two days a week in a residence, with no profit purpose, and barred the hiring of anyone under 18 (art. 1). It set an 8-hour day and 44-hour week, with overtime of at least 50% (art. 2), allowed the 12x36 shift pattern (art. 10) and dealt with accompanying the employer on trips, with a premium of at least 25% (art. 11), and with night work, with a premium of at least 20% (art. 14). It made inclusion in the FGTS severance fund compulsory (art. 21) and created a monthly deposit of 3.2% of pay as compensation for job loss (art. 22), which plays the role of the 40% penalty in the general regime. It created unemployment insurance for domestic workers, up to three instalments of one minimum wage (arts. 26 to 30) — the level that the 2026 law (item 3) would raise to six for rescued workers. And it set up the Simples Doméstico, a single unified payment slip (arts. 31 to 34), later operated through eSocial, which is a platform created by regulation and not by the text of the law.
marcos.autoria: Origem no Senado, PLS nº 224/2013 — Complementar, de autoria da Comissão Mista Permanente de Consolidação da Legislação Federal, e não de um parlamentar isolado nem do Executivo. Relator no Senado: Romero Jucá (PMDB-RR); na Câmara, onde tramitou como PLP nº 302/2013, o relator foi Arnaldo Faria de Sá (PTB-SP). Aprovada no Senado em 11/07/2013, na Câmara em 17/03/2015 e, com as alterações, de novo no Senado em 06/05/2015. Sancionada por Dilma Rousseff com dois vetos parciais (Mensagem 197/2015): a extensão do regime 12x36 a vigilantes e outras categorias, e a justa causa por ‘violação de fato ou circunstância íntima do empregador’, considerada ampla demais. O Congresso manteve os dois vetos em 24/09/2015.

seguranca_juridica.por: Repeals Law 5,859/1972 and puts in its place the whole domestic employment contract: who counts as a domestic worker under the more-than-two-days-a-week test, an 8-hour day with overtime of at least 50%, fixed-term contracts, FGTS dependent on later regulation, 120 days of transition, and an inspection procedure with a second visit.

concorrencia.por: Creates the Simples Doméstico, with taxes and FGTS collected in a single payment by the individual employer at rates set in the law, and makes inspection in the home conditional on prior appointment, with an advisory character and a second visit before any penalty. A compliance cost designed for the size of the employer.

fiscal.por: Creates the monthly deposit of 3.2% towards severance pay for dismissal without cause, unemployment benefit for domestic workers of one minimum wage for up to three months, and the Redom, a social-security recovery programme with a 120-day window to join.

marcos.numero_ato: Lei nº 15.455, de 1º de julho de 2026
marcos.nome: Direitos dos trabalhadores domésticos — 3 de 3: proteção a quem é resgatado de trabalho análogo ao de escravo
marcos.serie_item: protection for those rescued from work analogous to slavery
marcos.o_que_mudou: The law deals with domestic workers rescued from conditions analogous to slavery. It gives such a person priority in Bolsa Família benefits (art. 3) and sets the rescued worker's unemployment insurance at six instalments of one minimum wage (art. 5), against the three of the general level set by the 2015 law (item 2 of the sequence). It adds to Complementary Law 150/2015 a chapter of urgent protective measures (art. 30-A), with the victim's inclusion in the CadÚnico register and immediate institutional shelter, and orders the Maria da Penha Law to be applied where applicable — including its urgent protective measures — when the victim is a woman. Two points of precision matter here, because coverage usually gets them wrong: removing the abuser and barring contact are not commands of this law, they arrive by reference to the Maria da Penha Law and only when the victim is a woman; and the law raises no penalty and does not change art. 149 of the Penal Code — its only criminal change is to include the domestic employment relationship among the situations in § 9 of art. 129, which widens the reach of the aggravated offence without raising its range. It also waives the second-visit rule for labour inspection in cases of repeat offence, fraud or obstruction (art. 6) and sets a 48-hour deadline to report indications to the Labour Ministry and the Labour Prosecution Service (art. 7).
marcos.autoria: Projeto de Lei nº 5.760/2023, de autoria do deputado Reimont (PT-RJ), com relatoria de Benedita da Silva (PT-RJ) na Câmara e de Paulo Paim (PT-RS) no Senado. Aprovado na Câmara em 03/12/2024 e no Senado em 09/06/2026. Sancionado por Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva com um veto parcial (Mensagem 579/2026): caiu o dispositivo que exigia ordem judicial para incluir a vítima entre os beneficiários do seguro-desemprego. O veto amplia o acesso em vez de restringi-lo — a justificativa foi que a exigência judicial atrasaria o benefício. Não foi possível confirmar, nesta coleta, se o Congresso já apreciou esse veto.

seguranca_juridica.por: Brings the domestic employment relationship into the aggravated offence of art. 129, § 9 of the Penal Code, allows an infraction notice to be issued on the very first visit in cases of reduction to a condition analogous to slavery — an express exception to the two-visit rule of LC 150 — and requires the police authority to report evidence to the Ministry of Labour and to the Labour Public Prosecutor's Office within 48 hours.

fiscal.por: Gives priority in Bolsa Família to those who have been rescued, guarantees the rescued worker six unemployment insurance instalments of one minimum wage each and states that the expenditure will be met by social security budget appropriations of the Union.

acesso.disp: art. 8 (Chapter I-A and art. 30-A of LC 150/2015)
acesso.por: Creates emergency shelter and the victim's inclusion in the Cadastro Único, and orders the Lei Maria da Penha to be applied where the victim is a woman. One of the items of art. 30-A appears as vetoed in the official Planalto text.

nao_confirmados.por_que: Searches carried out in September 2026 indicate that the bill is still moving through the Congresso Nacional (approved in the Senado in 2024, under discussion in the Câmara dos Deputados), with no presidential sanction or publication on the Planalto site up to the date of this collection.

nao_confirmados.item: Law 11,445 of 5 January 2007 — Basic Sanitation Legal Framework, in its original wording
nao_confirmados.por_que: The page for the original text on the Planalto site returned only arts. 1 to 5 on every attempt, and the rest appeared only in the consolidated version — that is, already with the wording given by Law 14,026/2020. Classifying the 2007 law by provisions written in 2020 would credit one government with what another did, which is exactly the error this yardstick exists to avoid. The milestone stays in the list and on the timeline; what is missing is the classification by dimension, and it goes in when the original 2007 text can be checked in full.

notas: The full text of Lei 13.709/2018 (LGPD) available on planalto.gov.br could not be read through to the final signature block during this data collection (the reading tool's summary truncated before the end of the document); the information that Michel Temer signed the law with vetoes was corroborated by press coverage at the time (e.g.: Meio Bit, 'Temer sanciona, com vetos, a lei de proteção a dados pessoais'), but it was not verified directly in the Planalto signature block.

Decretos nº 12.975 and nº 12.976, both of May 20, 2026, were confirmed on the Planalto website: the first amends Decreto nº 8.771/2016 (the regulation of the Marco Civil da Internet) and expands the powers of the ANPD; the second sets guidelines for the protection of women against digital violence, including the blocking of unauthorized intimate content and safeguards against deepfakes generated by AI.

For some items (Lei 11.445/2007, Lei 14.273/2021, Lei 12.485/2011, Lei 13.257/2016, Lei 13.243/2016) it was not possible to confirm with precision the name of the member of Congress or the exact authorship of the originating bill within the scope of this collection; this is recorded in the 'autoria' field of each item, with no inference.

Lei 13.303/2016 (Lei das Estatais) was signed into law by Michel Temer while he was Vice-President acting as President, during Dilma Rousseff's suspension by the impeachment process (suspended on 12/05/2016, definitively removed on 31/08/2016); for that reason the administration in office at the signing was recorded as 'Temer (acting, May-Aug 2016)', distinct from Temer's full presidential term that began in August 2016.
No value judgment was made about the acts; the 'o_que_mudou' fields describe only what each act came to require, allow or prohibit, according to the official text read.

The four acts on the CARF casting vote are here as a sequence, not as loose facts, because the same rule was created, reversed and restored within fifteen years, by different governments and by different routes — a provisional measure, a parliamentary amendment, a provisional measure that lapsed, and a bill. Reading any one of them in isolation leads to misattribution: the 2020 tie-break in the taxpayer's favour did not come from the Executive, and the 2023 return of the casting vote was not decided by provisional measure but by a law passed in Congress and then altered when vetoes were overridden.

The three acts on domestic work are here as a sequence because their story only makes sense whole: the 2013 amendment equalised rights but left seven of them depending on a law; the 2015 complementary law made those seven enforceable; and the 2026 law created a regime of its own for those rescued from work analogous to slavery. None of the three originated in the Executive: the first two came from Congress and the third from a deputy's bill.

Three attributions of origin were corrected in September 2026, after checking the tramitation records of the Chamber and the Senate: the Early Childhood Legal Framework, the New Sanitation Framework and the Betting Law. The three errors had the same signature — mistaking a neighbouring actor or vehicle for the formal origin: a parliamentary front in place of the author, a rapporteur in place of the author and a shelved bill in place of the approved one, and a provisional measure that lapsed in place of the bill actually converted. The original error is described inside each of the three items, because erasing the correction would be worse than showing it.

criterios.o_que_mede: A milestone's radar measures REACH, not quality. Reach is the size of the change the text of the act makes in each dimension — how much it moves the rule, not whether it moved it for better or for worse. A milestone with reach 3 on public accounts may have improved or worsened the accounts: the radar does not answer that, and each dimension's detail says what is known and what is not.

escala.des: The text of the act creates no rule, alters none and repeals none in this dimension.
It moves something secondary — a deadline, a duty to report, an internal administrative power — without changing who may do what.
It creates or alters a right, a duty, a tax, a decision-making power or a barrier that applies across the sector.
It replaces the whole previous arrangement: a new regime, a new regulator, a new market or funding structure.

sinais.des: The act increases the right, the access, the entry, the revenue or the protection in this dimension.
The act reduces, conditions or raises the cost of what existed in this dimension.
The act transfers from one group to another without increasing or reducing the total.
Official sources disagree, or there is a pending court case on the point. The sign is left open and the detail says who argues what.

regras: The rating comes from the text of the act, checked against the official Planalto version, and every rating carries the provision that justifies it — article, paragraph or item. With no provision cited, the rating does not go in.
Expected effect does not count. If the rule changed, the reach is 2 or 3 even where the practical effect turned out to be nil. What is known about the effect goes in the detail, separately.

Measured effect goes elsewhere. Where this site holds an official series that bears on the dimension, it is cited with a link; where there is none, the detail says so, instead of leaving the reader to assume.
A rule that depends on later regulation keeps the reach of its text. The dependence does not lower the rating — it is recorded under legal certainty, which is where that fact matters.
The same yardstick applies to all 37 milestones, with no exception by government, by sector or by author.
Where two levels are both arguable, the lower one is used, and the detail says why the doubt exists.
criterios.indice: The weights you chose in the 'Weights of the dimensions' infographic produce a single number per milestone: the reach of each dimension multiplied by the weight you gave it, added up. It answers 'how much does this milestone move what matters to me' — and it does not answer, nor try to answer, whether the milestone is good. Two milestones with the same number can point in opposite directions; that is what the sign beside each dimension is for.

cobre.conta: Price or tariff to the end user, the rule for adjusting it, a subsidy paid directly to consumers, a coverage or universal-service obligation, an enforceable quality standard, continuity of the service.
cobre.nao_conta: A company's compliance cost, which belongs under competition and markets — unless the act itself orders the cost to be passed on to the price.

cobre.conta: Entry to and exit from the market, a licence or authorisation, a capital requirement, exclusivity and monopoly, the time it takes to start operating, regulatory cost in proportion to company size, the state's purchasing power.
cobre.nao_conta: The number of brands in the market, which is not the number of independent economic groups.

cobre.conta: Rules on long-term contracts, auctions and concessions, guarantees, amortisation periods, research and development incentives, construction licensing, workforce qualification.
cobre.nao_conta: Announced investment and merely potential capacity: until work is contracted or running, it is an intention, not a capability.

cobre.conta: Revenue, mandatory spending, tax breaks and exemptions, subsidies, federal guarantees, contingent liabilities, earmarked budget and fiscal rules.
cobre.nao_conta: A transfer of resources between groups, which is redistribution and shows as the '=' sign, not as the creation of wealth.

cobre.conta: Clarity of the text, transition periods, protection of vested rights and of contracts in force, who holds the power to decide, dependence on later regulation, the review procedure, penalties and the process for applying them, retroactive effect.
cobre.nao_conta: The volume of lawsuits, which depends on many things besides the rule.

cobre.conta: Who may restrict content, on what legal basis, by what procedure, within what deadline and with what possibility of challenge and redress; confidentiality and personal data where they affect what may be said; the press and advertising.
cobre.nao_conta: Removal by court order, by administrative act and at the platform's own initiative treated as the same thing — they are recorded separately.

criterios.estado: Classification in progress. The criteria above are settled and apply to every milestone; the milestones themselves are being classified one by one, and the counter below says how many are done. A milestone with no classification gets no provisional rating and no estimate: it simply does not appear in the comparator yet.

explicacao.o_que_e_lucro: It is the aggregate accounting net profit (or loss) of the federal state-owned companies: the sum of the bottom-line result of each company after all revenues, expenses, taxes and accounting items (including non-recurring gains and losses, such as exchange-rate variation, revaluation of equity holdings, court settlements, asset impairment). It is compiled and published by the Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos (MGI) from the companies' own financial statements, covering around 44 federal state-owned companies not dependent on the National Treasury, including the four large public banks and conglomerates (Petrobras, Banco do Brasil, BNDES, Caixa) and Eletrobras up to the privatization in 2022.
explicacao.o_que_e_primario: This is the primary balance of the federal state-owned companies in the Banco Central's fiscal statistics: the difference between non-financial revenues and expenditures (that is, not counting interest, not counting purely accounting items such as revaluation of assets or equity holdings). It is a fiscal cash-flow concept, used to measure the impact of state-owned companies on the consolidated public accounts (NFSP), and it covers a smaller universe of companies: since 2009 it excludes Petrobras and since 2010 it also excludes Eletrobras, besides never including the federal public banks (Banco do Brasil, Caixa, BNDES), which enter the fiscal statistics of the banking sector, not those of the non-financial state-owned companies.
explicacao.por_que_diferem: The two measures can point in opposite directions in the same year because they measure different things, in different universes of companies, with different criteria. The aggregate net profit (MGI) includes Petrobras — by far the largest contributor to the total in recent years — and the four large public banks/conglomerates, and it counts accounting gains that do not represent a cash inflow in the same period (for example, mark-to-market revaluation of equity holdings, such as those the BNDES holds in Petrobras and Vale, or large one-off provisions and write-downs, such as those recorded by Petrobras in 2014-2017). The Banco Central's primary balance, in turn, excludes precisely Petrobras (since 2009) and the public banks, and measures operating cash without interest — so that a year of record accounting profit for the state-owned companies as a whole (driven by Petrobras, BB, BNDES or Caixa) can coincide with a primary balance for the smaller set of state-owned companies (without those names) that is stable, negative or positive for entirely different reasons, such as the investment result of smaller companies (e.g.: Correios) or of state and municipal state-owned companies that are not part of this comparison. That is why the two series should never be added together or used as if they were the same thing measured twice.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Aggregate net profit of federal state-owned companies (MGI series) for the years 1998 to 2014 and for 2016
nao_encontrado.por_que: The publications found in this data collection (Boletim das Empresas Estatais Federais and Relatório Agregado das Empresas Estatais Federais, both from the MGI/former Ministério do Planejamento) cover, in a form accessible via WebSearch/WebFetch, mainly the period from 2017 on. Older publications, from the time when the now-extinct SEST (Secretaria de Coordenação e Controle das Empresas Estatais) published reports on the state-owned companies, were not found in a format accessible to the tools of this research (no access to curl/wget, only WebSearch and WebFetch).

nao_encontrado.o_que: Primary balance of federal state-owned companies in R$ millions (nominal value, not as % of GDP)
nao_encontrado.por_que: For the federal state-owned companies, the Banco Central publishes the primary balance series as a 12-month cumulative flow only as % of GDP (SGS 5790). There is a separate series in R$ millions, but only as a current monthly flow (SGS 4646, not cumulative over 12 months/the year); adding up the 12 monthly figures for each year would require an aggregate calculation made by this agent from raw data, which we prefer to avoid so as not to introduce a number that the Banco Central does not publish directly as such. For that reason, the estatais_primario series uses only the official metric as % of GDP.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Relatório Agregado das Empresas Estatais Federais 2024 (base year 2023), in full
nao_encontrado.por_que: The official URL of the PDF (gov.br/gestao/pt-br/central-de-conteudo/relatorios-das-estatais/relatorio_empresas_estatais_federais_2024.pdf) returned, when read by WebFetch, the generic gov.br institutional page instead of the content of the file, and an attempt via web.archive.org was blocked. The 2023 values used in this collection come from news reports citing that report, not from the original PDF.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Annex I — Séries Históricas of the Relatório Agregado das Empresas Estatais Federais 2025 (base year 2024), pages 82-103
nao_encontrado.por_que: The PDF (RelatrioEstataisFINAL2808WEB.pdf) is more than 100 pages long; the reading tool (WebFetch) processes the content with a smaller model that truncates very long documents, and the annex with the complete historical series falls outside the processed excerpt. The 2024 values used come from the body of the report (which was read) and from news reports about it, not from the annex.

nao_encontrado.o_que: BNDES standalone result in 2025 on an accounting/corporate basis (non-recurring)
nao_encontrado.por_que: In this collection only the release of the 2025 'recurring profit' (R$15,2 billion) by BNDES's own Agência BNDES de Notícias was located; the total book figure (which in years such as 2022 was much higher than the recurring one, because of gains on equity holdings marked to market) was not found in any source consulted.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Annual net profit/loss of Correios for the years 1998 to 2000 and 2001 to 2012 in exact figures
nao_encontrado.por_que: A news report (Gazeta do Povo) mentions that the Correios had a mostly positive result between 2001 and 2012, with the largest profit of the period in 2012 (R$1,86 billion in inflation-adjusted terms), but does not list the exact nominal value of each individual year within that interval in the text that could be read; for that reason those years were not included in the estatais_empresas series.

notas: None of the series in this file passes judgment on the cause or the merit of the results presented; the figures and the measurement criteria of each source are described, not the administration that produced them.

All values have a source that was read, with a URL, recorded in the 'obs' field of each point (series estatais_empresas) or in the 'notas'/'fonte' field of each series (estatais_lucro and estatais_primario). No value was estimated from memory.
The three series use criteria and company universes that differ from one another — see the 'criterio' field of each file before comparing or combining figures across them.

explicacao.o_que_e_desconto_associativo: Until April 2025, associations, unions and pensioners' organizations could sign Technical Cooperation Agreements with the INSS and deduct membership dues directly from the payroll of retirees and pensioners, subject to the beneficiary's authorization. Operation No Deduction, run by the Federal Police and the CGU and launched on 23 April 2025, investigates deductions made without that authorization.
explicacao.o_que_a_serie_mede: The total deducted per year, adding authorized and unauthorized deductions together. The CGU has published no monetary estimate of the irregular share; what exists are percentages from samples of interviews and document checks. Publishing the total is what makes the scale of the problem visible; calling it fraud is what the investigation does not yet license.
explicacao.desfecho_institucional: The deductions were suspended by INSS Decision Order No. 65, published at the end of April 2025 — two sources disagree between the 28th and the 29th. Law 15,327 of 6 January 2026 added paragraph 8 to article 115 of Law 8,213/1991 and barred these deductions outright, even with the beneficiary's express authorization, and further required full refund of any amount improperly deducted. The joint congressional inquiry into the INSS, seated on 20 August 2025, closed on 28 March 2026 with no final report approved: the rapporteur's report was rejected by 19 votes to 12 and the alternative report never came to a vote.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Value of association deductions in 2015 and earlier years
nao_encontrado.por_que: The extraction of the Maciça database carried out by the CGU in Report No. 1675291 covers January 2016 to May 2024. No official source with a figure earlier than 2016 was found, although the legal basis for the Technical Cooperation Agreements dates from 1991.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Annual total of association deductions in 2025
nao_encontrado.por_que: The deductions were suspended in April 2025 and no agency published the January-to-April total. The only monthly figure released is January 2025, at R$257.1 million.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Exact figure, with decimal places, for the 2024 realized amount
nao_encontrado.por_que: The available sources report only 'R$2.8 billion', rounded, attributed to CGU Report No. 1745585. The PDF of that report was not accessible in this collection: the eaud.cgu.gov.br portal blocks automated access and the copy held by the Chamber of Deputies returned an error.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Official estimate, in reais, of the irregular share of the deductions
nao_encontrado.por_que: The CGU expressly did not calculate it. The figures circulating to that effect are derived (the total multiplied by the interview percentage), not established by audit.
The INSS balance pages on gov.br returned restricted content and Agência Brasil is off the air under electoral-law restrictions during the 2026 election period.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Official text of the orders adjusting the contribution table from 1998 to 2007
nao_encontrado.por_que: There is no accessible public repository for these acts: the Planalto site does not publish ministerial orders and the old INSS archive blocks automated access. The values for that period come from secondary accounting compilations cross-checked against each other.

nao_encontrado.o_que: Normative act that would have suspended the reduced rates between June 2002 and March 2003
nao_encontrado.por_que: Three compilations record a return to the three full rates in that interval and a fourth does not. Constitutional Amendment 37/2002 does not mention the provision that created the reduction — on the contrary, it extends the law containing it. Since the divergence could not be settled against a primary source, that interval is not asserted in the text of this infographic.

contagens_impostos.titulo: The published tallies — and why they do not match

grupos.rotulo: How many tax-raising measures under Lula III, according to each tally
itens: 24 — Gazeta do Povo, 30/05/2025. Counts each creation or increase announced between January 2023 and 22/05/2025, including proposals still going through Congress. Sums it up as “one increase every 37 days”.
37 — Exame, 17/06/2025. Counts government acts and proposals already approved by Congress that raise the burden: decrees, provisional measures and laws, from 2023 to June 2025.
27 — Poder360, 09/10/2025. A narrower criterion: only major taxes that raised revenue consistently for some period. One-off measures are left out.
30 — Estadão, Duquesa de Tax column, 09/03/2026. It is a fact-check of the claim of 38 made by senator Flávio Bolsonaro; the author arrives at 30. The full list was published as a video.

36 (or 43) — Gazeta do Povo, 29/03/2026. Thirty-six measures actually enacted, plus 5 proposals that lapsed with Provisional Measure 1,303/2025 and 2 of a non-tax nature, adding up to 43 revenue-raising initiatives in 38 months.

37 — Ranking dos Políticos, 07/04/2026. A site with a declared position, not a journalistic outlet. Its own text concedes that, without the proposals still in Congress and without import tariffs, the count falls to 25 or 27.
38 — senator Flávio Bolsonaro, March 2026. A political statement, with no published criteria.

The same thing counted by seven different rulers gives anywhere from 24 to 43. The difference is almost entirely methodological: do proposals that never became law count? do measures that lapsed count? do the tax-reform substitutions count? up to what date is the count made?

All the tallies above are of the Lula III administration. No equivalent tally, made with the same criteria, exists for Bolsonaro, Temer, Dilma, Lula I-II or FHC — and so no comparison between administrations can be drawn from them.
No outlet has published the tally of the other side: how many tax-cutting measures the same administration took. The asymmetry belongs to the available material, not to the facts.
We found no publication that supports the figure of 47, which circulates on social media. The published tallies run from 24 to 43.
It was about 4,000 products, not 4,000 taxes. The 2022 linear cut in the industrial-products tax reached that many product codes in the tax schedule (the TIPI), by way of a single decree.
Brazil has somewhere around three dozen federal taxes — seven of them taxes proper and the rest fees and contributions. Cutting 4,000 federal taxes would be arithmetically impossible.
If the same ruler were applied to both sides, either both administrations count decrees, or both count the items affected. Mixing the two units is what produces the gap between “27” and “4,000”.
Leaving the income-tax brackets frozen while wages rise increases the tax paid without anyone signing anything. The exemption threshold stayed at R$ 1,903.98 from 2015 to 2022.
The reverse as well: the zero PIS/Cofins rate on diesel ended on 1 January 2024 because the deadline set in Law 14,592/2023 expired, with no new act.
Counting normative acts measures who acts by decree and by law, not who charges more. Whoever lets the rule run by itself appears on no tally at all.

contagens_impostos.nota: Each tally is identified by outlet and date because the date changes the number: Gazeta do Povo doubled its own count, from 24 to 43, in ten months. Tallies from outlets with a declared political position are marked as such and are not treated here as equivalent to data journalism or to an official source.

estatais_lista.nota: Names as they appear in the SEST register. Joining the list almost never means a new state company created for public policy: of the 41 entries since 1990, most are subsidiaries or corporate vehicles of Petrobras, Banco do Brasil and Caixa. The ones created as policy instruments are few and can be named: Conab (1990), EMGEA (2001), EPE and Hemobrás (2004), EBC (2007), Ceitec (2008), Ebserh (2011), ABGF (2012), Amazul and PPSA (2013), NAV Brasil (2020) and ENBPar (2021) — this last one created precisely to take over the nuclear plants and Itaipu when Eletrobras was denationalized. On the other side, leaving the list is not a synonym for privatization either: the register dates the exit but does not standardize the reason, and sale of control, absorption by another state company, liquidation and transfer all sit together there. The clearest case is right at the start of the series: Cobal, Cibrazem and CFP leave in 1991 because they were merged to form Conab, which joins in the same period — three exits and one entry, and no sale.

dimensoes.des: Cost to the user, coverage, availability, quality and continuity of the service. A company's compliance cost is not the same thing as the final price: pass-through is a hypothesis to be checked, not an automatic consequence.
Entry, exit, expansion, capital barriers, time to start operating and regulatory cost in proportion to company size. The number of brands is not the number of independent economic groups.

Additional investment, infrastructure built and in operation, productivity, employment, income and innovation. Potential capacity is not existing operation, and investment after a rule is not, by itself, an effect of it.

Revenue actually received, spending, tax breaks, subsidies, guarantees and contingent liabilities. Transferring resources is not creating wealth, and more revenue does not demonstrate a better service.

Clarity of the rules, stability over time, transition, decision-making powers, dependence on regulation, contractual protection and review procedures. Fewer lawsuits does not on its own demonstrate more predictability.

Who can restrict, on what legal basis, by what procedure, within what deadline and with what possibility of challenge and redress. Removal by court order, by administrative act and at the platform's own initiative are different things; protection against harm and the risk of undue restriction are recorded separately.
